detailed_description: The Case Converter turns pasted text into common casing formats such as uppercase, lowercase, title case, sentence case, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and kebab-case. It is useful when preparing labels, variable names, URL slugs, headings, or copied text that needs consistent casing. The conversion runs directly in the browser and each result can be copied separately. Some transformations use simple JavaScript rules, so users should review acronyms, names, and language-specific casing before publishing.
usage_steps: Paste or type the text you want to convert.
Choose the format that matches your target use case.
Click Copy beside the result you want.
Check proper names, abbreviations, and non-English text before publishing.
Repeat with new input when you need another conversion.
usage_examples: Convert a heading into uppercase for a design mockup.
Turn a phrase into snake_case for a configuration key.
Create kebab-case text for a URL slug.
Change pasted all-caps text into a more readable sentence case draft.

faqs.question: Which case formats are available?
faqs.answer: The page provides uppercase, lowercase, title case, sentence case, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and kebab-case outputs.

faqs.question: Can I copy only one converted result?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each generated result has its own copy button.

faqs.question: Will title case handle every style guide perfectly?
faqs.answer: No. The conversion is a practical browser rule, so review articles, prepositions, acronyms, and names for your preferred style.

faqs.question: Is this useful for code identifiers?
faqs.answer: Yes. camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and kebab-case are handy for variables, components, filenames, and config keys.

faqs.question: Does the tool store my text?
faqs.answer: The visible conversion happens in the browser page. Avoid pasting confidential content on shared or untrusted devices.
